_meta.what_this_is: A single-server task queue over 12 ticks. A high-priority task (priority 5) arrives every tick, and one low-priority task L (priority 1) arrives at tick 0. The server completes one task per tick and chooses which by priority. STRICT priority always serves the highest-priority task available, so with a high-priority task arriving every tick the low task L is never the highest and is starved forever. AGING raises a waiting task effective priority by its wait time, so L eventually out-prioritizes freshly-arrived high tasks and gets served -- with a bounded wait.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The arrival stream (a high task every tick plus one low task at tick 0) is hand-authored so strict priority never serves L within the horizon while aging serves it at tick 4. Every scheduling decision is computed in aging.py.
_meta.format: horizon: number of ticks (one task served per tick); tasks: [{id, priority, arrival}]. Aging adds wait-time to priority.
